488	`;%TYPE`, a negative offset stepping the other way; a pattern that can't be one left out with why) for the dialog and for the
489	`import_fill_patterns` and `export_fill_patterns` commands. A PAT file is hostile input: `read` stops after `MAX_PATTERNS`
490	(2,000) patterns and counts the rest, `Read::left_out` names the first `MAX_LEFT_OUT` (100) with `left_out_count` for all, a line
491	is cut at 22 fields and a bad one is echoed to 40 letters, a family whose dashes are all spaces is left out, and a file over
492	`MAX_TEXT` (16 MiB) is refused unread. A byte that isn't UTF-8 is read as the Latin-1 letter with its number, which is right
493	for accents and not for Windows-1252's punctuation at 0x80 to 0x9F. The description after a pattern's name isn't kept. The
494	`import_fill_patterns` command takes the file's `text` up to that size too (a name is limited to 256 letters, a file isn't) and
495	replies with the first 100 `left_out` and `left_out_count`.
496	
497	Edit Type opens a region's Type Properties from either a selected region or an active sketch: select a type, create a
498	new one, duplicate one with its settings, or rename it. Foreground and background each have their own pattern (including
499	None) and color; masking controls whether paper hides geometry underneath. The combined preview shows both layers and
500	a sample line behind them, so masking can be checked before applying. The Patterns tab edits and creates patterns in
501	the same draft. Apply and OK update definitions and the selected instances in one transaction; a type edit affects every
502	region of that type, a duplicate is assigned only to the selected instances or the active sketch, and Cancel discards
503	unapplied work. Duplicate or blank names are refused without replacing another definition. Renames preserve library
504	identity and update the active sketch's type reference. The palette's Type Selector and Edit Type use the same region
505	types as the Options Bar.
506	
507	The instance parameter grid has no second Region Type field: the Type Selector is the type control. Non-masking regions
508	replace model backgrounds while retaining visible cut outlines, cut foreground patterns (including solid foregrounds),
509	and projected model lines. `render/regions.rs` finds the drawing's ink once (the model layer's lines and patterns, less what a
510	later fill covers, so a low wall hidden by a cut wall does not reappear; and a section's or elevation's hidden-line picture as
511	runs of its pixels, which is all the ink an elevation has) and gives each region the part of it in its area: the outline less
512	its holes, inside an odd number of rings, less the masking regions drawn before it. A line is kept where it lies in the area or
513	within half its stroke of it (its pen's width as it will draw, from the owner's object style while the pen is not set yet), so a
514	region edge sketched on a wall face keeps the whole face; Visibility/Graphics weights wider than the object style's are not
515	allowed for. Lines are cut by the rings and the masks as they are, never by boolean operations on polygons (which are cubic in
516	the corners an outline can have): only the model's filled patterns are, by the pieces of the area they reach. The pieces of a
517	polyline that meet stay one line, so its corners keep their joins, and a dashed line's dashes stay where they were (the dashes of
518	the cycle a piece begins in are solid lines of their own). A section's ink belongs to the region that keeps it (`Part::Pattern`),
519	so a sheet's viewport, which keeps what an element owns, has it. A caller that has the section's picture (the desktop's, a sheet's,
520	`section_png`'s) hands it in (`render::section_over`, `section_at_over`), at the view's size or a multiple of it (a screen with more
521	pixels to the point), and the ink is the picture's own pixels, as runs: a row of a pixel's height, and a run of up to two pixels
522	that sits on one of the row above (the edge of a tall wall) joined to it as one vertical line, so 200 walls 20 m tall at 4000 x 2600
523	px are some hundreds of lines and not a million runs. A picture of more than 250,000 runs (noise, not drawings) keeps the first
524	250,000 and the drawing's `notes` say the ink of the last rows is under the region. `render::section` draws a picture of its own
525	when a non-masking region wants one, which costs what the picture does, every call. Masking still hides the model; detail annotation remains above the
526	region. The same display list feeds the desktop, PNG, SVG and sheet viewports.
527	
528	Limits, kept as Revit has them or not yet built: a non-masking region with a solid background hides a room's tag text while its outlines
529	stay (Revit keeps room tags above filled regions: not verified); grids, levels and room fills are drawn before the regions, so a masking
530	region hides them; there is no Bring to Front or Send to Back, a region is over the model and under the annotation, in the order of its
531	id; Move and Rotate carry a region's or a floor's model pattern with it (`pattern_origin`), where Revit may leave a model pattern fixed in
532	the building, and Align moves it; a filled region drawn on a sheet itself is plain annotation over the viewports, so a solid one hides
533	what lies under it (Revit has no regions on sheets).
534	
535	Sketch snapping (`snap::in_sketch`) combines the visible model's wall faces and slab edges, detail lines and existing
536	region boundaries in the active view, and the draft's own lines. It supports endpoints, midpoints (of each segment of a
537	polyline), intersections (where two walls meet is one too), perpendiculars, nearest points and angle guides, the anchors of
538	annotation (a note's insertion point and leader, a tag's head, a dimension's stations, a spot elevation, section and elevation
539	marks, detail groups and repeating details), and a camera's eye and target rather than its mark's body or name, honoring Manage > Snaps
540	and one-point overrides. An element being edited is omitted as a model snap target; its draft supplies the boundary instead.
541	Rectangle and arc previews use the same origin points and Shift constraint as a click. Annotation in another independent view,
542	or hidden by Visibility/Graphics, is excluded. A plan view cuts where its own view range says (`plan_range` of the view, not of its
543	level); a section or an elevation has no plan to snap to, only its own detail lines and regions. Of what the plan builds, the
544	nearest `MAX_OUTLINES` elements within reach have their outlines snapped to (one `walls::Index` for them all), and the nearest
545	`MAX_NEAR` chords are tried against each other. Ceilings snap in a floor plan as well as a ceiling plan, because a snap does not know
546	which of the two the cursor is in, and the members of a detail group are not snap targets.
547	
548	The reference workflows are Autodesk's [fill layers](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2024/ENU/Revit-GetStarted/files/GUID-8A38ADC8-98A6-4A30-BD21-1886F044F6ED.htm),
549	[region editing](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2026/ENU/Revit-DocumentPresent/files/GUID-183D9B1E-6554-4C19-9EA9-B32C8D2A5C9D.htm),
550	and [sketch snaps](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2022/ENU/Revit-Customize/files/GUID-A3947840-1F30-41D7-AF75-B61687952A07.htm).
551	Boundary weights follow each boundary line's style. See also Autodesk's [region masking behavior](https://www.autodesk.com/support/technical/article/caas/sfdcarticles/sfdcarticles/Filled-Region-with-solid-fill-does-not-cover-all-elements-in-Revit.html).
552	
553	A material's cut and surface may be one of the project's fill patterns (`Material::cut_pattern`, `surface_pattern`, a
554	library reference like a region type's), over the patterns drawn in code (`model::Pattern`), which stay for the materials
555	that name them: `material` takes either name for `cut` and `surface`, and the desktop's material editor lists both. A fill
556	pattern a material shows can't be deleted, and is renamed with it. `render::fill_pattern` draws a fill pattern for a
557	region, a cut layer (its courses along the layer) and a floor's or a ceiling's surface. A model pattern is aligned and
558	rotated as Revit's: a filled region and a floor hold `pattern_origin` and `pattern_angle` (`fills::strokes_placed`), which
559	Move, Rotate and Mirror carry with the element; Align with a pattern line picked second (`render::pattern_line_at`) moves the
560	origin so that line lies on the reference, and Properties shows Pattern Angle. `Model::align_pattern(id, reference, line)` is
561	that arithmetic (the origin moved across by the gap between the two parallel lines, to the micron; the error says when the
562	element has no model pattern, or the lines aren't parallel or have no length), so every front end gets the same answer and
563	sets it with `modify`. `pattern_origin` and `pattern_angle` are in the `modify`, `filled_region` and `floor` command docs, and
564	`elements` shows them for a region and a floor even at their defaults.
565	
566	## Linked models
567	
568	A `Link` element (`link.rs`; commands `link` and `reload`) is another project shown in this one as a reference. The file holds its name, its
569	path, where its origin stands (`at`) and a turn (`angle`); what it read is `Model::loaded`, by path, outside the file (`serde(skip)`), filled by
570	`link`, `reload` and `open` (`relink`, which doesn't follow the links of a linked file). The views draw `link::seen(model)`: the project with
571	each loaded link's built elements (`built`: not its views, sheets, annotation, detail lines, filled regions, detail groups, rooms, grids or links) moved and turned by `commands::transformed`
572	and brought in with `insert::insert_as(.., linked: true)` under ids from `LINKED` up (`ids.rs`), so `link::is_linked(id)` tells them; a level of the
573	link at the height of one of the project's (1 mm) is that level, another comes in named `link: level`. Everything that takes a `&Model` draws and snaps to
574	them without knowing: `Look::with` makes a linked id halftone, and picking never answers one (`Drawing::pick_all`, `in_box`, `Image::pick`,
575	`in_box`, `shows` and `Mesh::pick` leave them out). The commands that make an image (`render`, `save` to svg, png or pdf) draw `seen`; the desktop's
576	`view_model` does, cached by the project's `Arc`. The schedules, `Model::check`, IFC and every command that edits work on the project itself.
577	To do: shared coordinates, a link's graphics overrides and visibility per view, hosting on a linked wall, unloading.
578	
579	## Dimensions
580	
581	A dimension (`Dimension`, the `dimension` command) measures the model as it is, so it follows what it measures. Its `refs` are lines
582	(`Reference {id, face}`: a wall's centre line, faces and ends, a door's or window's centre and jambs, a grid, a straight detail line) or, with
583	`point: start|end`, the point at that end of one (`Model::reference_point`: a wall's centre line ends where its location line does, a face where
584	the outline turns off it, so at the mitred corner; a detail line of any shape at its ends; `reference_points` lists them, `endpoint_at` finds the
585	nearest, `{endpoint: [x, y]}` in a command). `reference_geometry` gives either as a line, a point as a line of no length, and `crossings` lays
586	them along the way the dimension measures (`measured_along`): a linear one's `orient` (horizontal or vertical), else square to its first line,
587	else from its first point to the next elsewhere. `Model::check` refuses a line not parallel to the first, or not square to a linear one's line,
588	and points all in one place. Mirror keeps the end of a line along the element and flips the one across it (`Reference::mirrored`); Flip swaps
589	both. A linear one given no `orient` runs vertical where `at` is east or west of everything it measures, else horizontal; the desktop's Auto
590	(`dims::Placing::kind`) also lays an aligned one where the cursor is among the points (`Orient::follow`), as Archicad does. Radial and diameter
591	dimensions measure round columns, curved walls (centre line or a face) and circles and arcs (`reference_arc`); arc length, a curved wall's or an
592	arc's length along it (`reference_sweep`), all of it or, with two point references after the arc, between them (`Model::arc_span`), its line an arc through `at` round the same centre. `dims::round_at` picks the face nearest a click.
593	
594	Each dimension has a dimension type (`dims.rs`, `Model::dimension_types`, a library entry `Kind::DimensionType`, the `dimension_type` command),
595	Revit's type parameters with lengths in mm on paper: Dimension String Type (continuous, baseline, ordinate), tick mark (diagonal, arrow, open
596	arrow, dot, none) and its size, line and tick pens, colour, dimension line extension, Witness Line Control (gap to element, or fixed to the
597	dimension line with its length), witness line gap and extension, baseline spacing, centre marks, and its text: font (as text types take one,
598	`DimensionType::lettering`), size, bold, italic, underline, width factor, offset, opaque or transparent background, Read Convention, units and
599	rounding (`DimensionType::length`), and the radius and diameter symbols and the equality text. A project starts with `Diagonal - 2.5mm Arial`,
600	which aligned, linear, angular and arc length dimensions start in, and `Arrow - 2.5mm Arial`, which radial and diameter ones do
601	(`dims::default_type`); a file of format 9 gives its dimensions their kind's (`Model::typed_dimensions`). A dimension's own text, Revit's
602	instance values, is a prefix, a suffix, text above and below, Replace With Text and Equality Display, and a segment may have its own over it
603	(`texts`, `SegmentText`, the `dimension_text` command; `Dimension::text` reads one through the other, `dimension_segment_at` finds a segment by a
604	point); `Model::dimension_labels` is what its
605	numbers read (and `elements` shows as `labels`): a baseline string's each from its first reference, an ordinate's each witness line's, the first 0.
606	An aligned or linear dimension may be kept equal (`equal`, Revit's EQ, which also turns its Equality Display on) and have segments
607	locked at a length (`locked`, `Lock`; the `dimension_constraint` command). `constraints::keep` runs in `Session::execute` after every undoable
608	command, before the check: each constrained dimension is solved on its own line (its `stations`, each with its reference), a locked segment tying
609	two stations rigidly and equality tying all its segments to one length (a locked one's, else its ends', which stay where they are, so an inner
610	reference dragged goes back); a run of tied stations stays where what the command moved puts it, else where its first is. What has to move is
611	moved by `commands::move_by`, as `move` moves it, and the dimensions are solved again (`PASSES`) until all hold; where they can't (locked
612	lengths that differ made equal, one element pulled two ways), the command is refused, saying which dimension, and nothing changes.
613	A length typed for a segment (`dimension_value`; in the window, a click on the selected dimension's number, as a temporary
614	dimension's takes one) moves what the segment ends at, its second station's reference, along the dimension by the difference
615	(`move_by`), and a locked segment is locked at it; the other locks then hold or the command is refused. Align with `lock` (Revit's
616	padlock: in the window, the open padlock Align offers on the line it moved) leaves a lock: a dimension of the aligned line's reference
617	and the reference's (`to`, else whatever has a line along it), its one segment locked at 0 and `alignment` set, which
618	`constraints::keep` holds as it holds the others, so the two lines stay on one line whatever either is moved by; one that can't hold
619	with the other locks is refused, and the project is as it was. A lock is drawn by a front end, never on paper (`render/dimensions.rs`
620	draws nothing of it): the window shows each locked segment's shut padlock whether its dimension is selected or not, and each alignment
621	lock's padlock beside where its lines meet, which a click unlocks (deletes). Format 15 holds them; 14 would read one as a dimension of
622	nothing.
623	`render/dimensions.rs` draws them all as the type says (`Ink`: its lines, ticks and witness lines, and its numbers laid out by `crate::text`
624	over the paper where the background is opaque).
625	
626	A 3D view has dimensions of its own (`Element::Dimension3D`, the `dimension_3d` command; `dims3d.rs`), as Revit's aligned dimension in a 3D
627	view: two references (`Ref3`), each a point of the model or a point on an edge (its two ends with it), and a point its line passes through,
628	kept by the view (`view`, a GUID: deleting the view takes them with it) and of a dimension type as a plan's are. Between two points it measures
629	straight from one to the other; to an edge, square to the edge's line, so between two parallel edges it is how far apart they are
630	(`dims3d::ends`). They hold places in space, not references to elements: moving an element leaves them, and `move`, `rotate` and `mirror`
631	take them in plan when they are moved themselves. They draw as marks (`dims3d::marks`, `Mark`: a polyline in the picture's pixels, its width
632	and colour), through any camera and at any paper size (`SCREEN` pixels a paper millimetre on screen, `sheet::DENSITY` on a sheet): a
633	witness line from each end of what it measures to its line, its line, a tick at each end and its number lettered along it in our strokes
634	(`font.rs`), reading from the left, on the side away from what it measures; nothing hides them. `dims3d::paint` paints marks into the
635	processor's picture, which the `render` command does for a 3D view; a sheet draws them as its own lines over the view's picture, so they print
636	in its PDF; the window draws them over the picture on either painter (the card's too) with the theme's ink, the selection's colour when
637	picked. Visibility/Graphics hides them with Dimensions (`category_of`). In the window the Aligned Dimension tool (DI) in the 3D view picks a
638	corner seen within the snap's reach (`Scene::corner_near`), else an edge within a pick's (`Scene::edge_near`, the point of it nearest the
639	cursor), else the point of the face there; after two, a click places the line where it meets the plane through the two that faces the
640	camera most (`dims3d::line_through`), and the status line says how long it is. In Modify a click on a dimension's lines picks it before what
641	the picture shows under them (`dims3d::pick`).

level | {elevation, name?, extent?: [[x,y],[x,y]]} a level at an elevation in mm; `extent`, the rectangle in plan its plane stretches over (south-west corner, then north-east), where sections, elevations and the 3D view show it (without one, the model's, a metre past it)

grid | {start: [x,y], end: [x,y], name?} names follow the last grid: 1, 2… or A, B…

wall | {points: [[x,y],…], closed?, type?, level?, top_level?, top_offset?, height?, base_offset?, arc?, location?, attach_top?, attach_base?, room_bounding?} one wall per segment of its location line; up to the next level, or `height` mm tall (unconnected), or up to `top_level`, `top_offset` mm above it (0; negative, below it; the top must stay above the base). `arc`: degrees each turns from its start to its end, counter-clockwise (180, a half circle bulging to its right). `location`: the line of it the points are on: centre (the default), core-centre, exterior-finish, interior-finish, exterior-core or interior-core; its exterior side is to the left of its start to its end, so walls drawn clockwise face out. `attach_top`, `attach_base`: a roof or floor its top follows from below, or its base stands on. `room_bounding`: false for a wall rooms run past (a low wall, a balustrade); true, the default, bounds them

door | {at: [x,y] | wall: id, offset?, type?, family?, level?, mark?, flip_facing?, flip_hand?} in the wall under `at`, or in `wall` centred `offset` mm from its start; with `family`, a door family's `type` (its first by default), which sizes the opening and draws the door

window | {at: [x,y] | wall: id, offset?, sill?, type?, family?, level?, mark?, flip_facing?} like door; `sill` defaults to the type's (a family's `Sill Height`)

floor | {boundary?: [[x,y],…], openings?: [[[x,y],…],…] | sketch?: [[[x,y],[x,y]],…], level?, type?, offset?, slope?, arrow?: [[x,y],[x,y]], structural?} a slab (a structural one with `structural`, as Revit's Floor: Structural), its top at the level, or `offset` mm above it, open through `openings` (holes inside it, apart); no boundary = the outline of the level's walls along their centre lines, open over each loop of them standing free inside, joined to none of the outer ones and with no room in it (a courtyard). Sloped: its top rises `slope` degrees (negative, falls) along the slope arrow, from its tail, where it's at the offset, toward its head. Its top's model pattern starts at `pattern_origin` and turns by `pattern_angle` (see modify). An outline, and each opening, is simple: no edge across another or along it, none ending part way along one, no spike or keyhole slit (`ceiling`, `roof` and `shaft` too, and `modify`, `move` and `edit_boundary` of any of them: they are refused, saying which edges); a file that has one still opens, and works until a command changes its outline

room | {point: [x,y], level?, name?, number?, top_level?, limit_offset?, base_offset?, frozen?} bounded by the walls and the room separation lines around the point (walls the level's `computation_height` cuts; separation lines whatever their height). Placed where nothing encloses it, or in a space another room has (two rooms can't share one; the first keeps it), it is placed unbounded, a 1000 mm square, and the reply has a `warning`. Its height is Revit's: from `base_offset` mm over its level (0) up to `limit_offset` mm over its upper limit `top_level` (null: Not Bounded, over its own level). Unless given, 300 mm under the level above (`top_level` that level, `limit_offset` -300), or with none above, not bounded and 2500 mm tall. `elements` gives its `unbounded_height` and `volume_m3`, its area times that height. `frozen` (a yes or no; also `modify {id, frozen}`) keeps the boundary the room has now: it keeps its size whatever the walls do, and the walls are never searched for it again, which saves time in a project of many rooms. Unfrozen, it follows the walls again. Only an enclosed room can be frozen

column | {at: [x,y], type?, angle?, level?, top_level?, height?, base_offset?} a column, its width along `angle` degrees; up to the next level, or `height` mm tall, or up to `top_level`

roof | {level?, boundary?: [[x,y],…], courtyards?: [[[x,y],…],…] | sketch?: [[[x,y],[x,y]],…], slope?, slopes?: [degrees, …], overhang?, gables?: [edge, …], gable?, offset?, extrusion?, openings?: [[[x,y],…],…], join?, type?} a roof on `level` (by default the one above the lowest), its base `offset` mm above it. Over `boundary` or else the walls of the level below, `overhang` mm (500) past their faces, round any `courtyards` (holes in it, inside it and apart, with eaves of their own; over the walls, by default each loop of them standing free inside, joined to none of the outer ones and with no room in it): flat at `slope` 0, else every edge sloping up at `slope` degrees (30), hips, valleys and ridges where the slopes meet, but the edges in `gables` (edge i runs from point i to the next, the courtyards' edges numbered on after the boundary's) left upright, gable ends; `gable` leaves a rectangle's short ends upright. `slopes`: a slope in degrees (up to 75) for each edge, numbered as `gables` are, 0 for an edge that takes `slope`; none, every edge does; the eaves stay level and an edge in `gables` stays upright whatever its slope. A `sketch` line may carry a `slope` for the edges along it. Or with `extrusion` {line: [[x,y],[x,y]], profile: [[along, up],…], from?, to}: its underside's profile in the upright plane through `line`, along it from its start and up from the base, swept square to it from `from` (0) to `to` mm to its left. `openings` are holes through it in plan; with `join`, a

dimension | {refs: [ref, …], at: [x, y], level?, kind?: aligned|linear|angular|radial|diameter|arc_length, orient?: horizontal|vertical} aligned (the default): the distances between parallel references, along a line through `at` (between points, along the first two; points and lines, square to the lines); linear: the same with its line horizontal or vertical as `orient` says, or without one as `at` lies: east or west of the points, vertical, else horizontal (its lines must run square to it); angular: the angle between two references that meet, on the side of `at`; radial: a round column's, curved wall's, circle's or arc's radius, toward `at`; diameter: the same across, through its centre; arc_length: how long a curved wall's centre line or face, or an arc, is along it (all of it, or with two point refs after it, between them), its line an arc through `at`. A ref is {id, face?}: a wall's centre (the default), left or right face (of its start-to-end direction), start or end; a door's or window's centre, or its jamb toward its wall's start or end; a grid's line; a straight detail line, or its start or end (radial: a circle or an arc of one). With `point: start|end`, {id, face?, point} is the point at that end of the line: a wall's centre line's end, a face's corner, a grid's, a detail line's (of any shape) or a jamb's end. Or a point [x, y] on one of those lines (for radial and diameter, on a round edge; for arc_length, on the arc), or {endpoint: [x, y]}, the end of one nearest it, within 1

text | {text, at: [x, y], view?, type?, angle?, leader?: [x, y], override_format?, runs?: [{from, to, bold?, italic?, underline?}, …]} a text note, its first line's top left at `at`, in a view by name or id: a level's plan (the lowest by default; `at` in plan mm), a section or an elevation (`at` along its line from its start, and up), or a sheet by number (`at` in paper mm). Lettered as its text `type` says (2.5mm unless told; `text_type` lists and makes them: its font, its size, its border), turned `angle` degrees counter-clockwise; with `leader`, a line to that point. Lines break at \n. With `override_format`, each run makes characters `from` up to `to` (counted in characters, a line break one) bold, italic or underlined (true), or not (false), whatever the type says; they stay when the type changes, and `modify` with a new `text` alone keeps them on what didn't change. Font and size are the type's

spot | {at: [x, y], view?, host?} a spot elevation: in a level's plan (the lowest by default), the height of the top of what stands on the level at `at` (or of `host`), following it; in a section or an elevation, of its point `at`, along and up

tag | {ids?: [id,…], label?, level?, category?, offset?: [dx, dy], leader?} tags elements with a field of theirs: a door's or window's mark, a room's name, else the type, or `label`, any field its category's schedule has (`Height`, `Area`, a project parameter); doors, windows, walls, columns, components, floors, ceilings, roofs, rooms, runs and stairs. `offset` mm from the point it names (beside the wall for a door or window, else up and right); without ids, every door and window on the level not tagged yet, or of `category`

copy | {ids: [id,…], by: [dx, dy]} copies elements, with the doors and windows of copied walls; returns the copies' ids

rotate | {ids: [id,…], about: [x, y], angle, copy?} turns elements about a point by `angle` degrees, counter-clockwise; walls joined to them stay joined, and doors and windows turn with their walls

mirror | {ids: [id,…], axis: [[x, y], [x, y]], copy?} mirrors elements across the line through two points; mirrored doors and windows face the other way

filled_region | {sketch: [[[x,y],[x,y]],…], view?, type?, line_style?: name | null} a filled region in a view (a plan, a section, an elevation or a sheet, in its own terms; the lowest plan by default): the loops its sketch closes into (see `sketch`: any number of outlines, a loop inside one a hole, one inside that an island), filled as type `type` (Solid Black unless told) says, its boundary in line style `line_style` (Thin Lines unless told; null, unseen: a masking region's way). It draws over the model, under the annotation; edit its sketch with edit_boundary. A model pattern starts at the region's `pattern_origin` and turns by its `pattern_angle` (see modify)

create_group | {ids, name?} a detail group made of detail lines, filled regions and text notes of one view, as Revit's Create Group: they become type `name`'s members (Group 1, 2… unless told), and one group of it takes their place, its origin the middle of them. Place it again with detail_group; ungroup gives its members back. Returns {id, name}

detail_line | {view?, style?, and a curve: `points` [[x, y], …] (with `arcs`, each segment's turn in degrees counter-clockwise, and `closed`), `start` and `end` (with `arc` degrees or a `through` point), `centre` and `radius` (a circle), `centre` and `radii` [a, b] (an ellipse, with `angle` degrees and `span` [from, to] degrees for part of one), `control` [[x, y], …] (a spline by its control points, with `knots`), or `fit` [[x, y], …] (a spline through them, with `start_tangent` and `end_tangent`)} a detail line in a view, by name or id, in the view's own terms: a level's plan (the lowest by default; plan mm), a section or an elevation (along its line from its start, and up) or a sheet by number (paper mm). It draws in line style `style` (Thin Lines unless told), only in its view, and goes with it; with `insulation`, a width in mm, it draws as batt insulation along its curve, as Revit's Insulation; with `centre_mark` true, a small cross marks the centre of its arcs, circle or ellipse; with `cloud`, an arc length in mm, it draws as a revision cloud's scallops along it (outward round a loop, a scallop ending at each corner), of `revision` (any text, a label kept with the cloud and listed by `elements`; nothing else reads it); a line is insulation or a cloud, not both. An arc, a circle or an ellipse lies within 1,000 km of the origin (an arc of 359.9999999999° is a circle of radius 5.7e14 mm, and is refused), and a polyline's arcs take no more than 8,192 points to draw within 0.25 mm: 10,000 

schedule | {name?, category?, categories?, fields?, filters?, sort?, grouped?, path?} a schedule view, as Revit's View > Schedules makes one, and its table: columns, rows, the `elements` each row lists, and totals (and a .csv file with a path, or an .xlsx workbook for a path ending .xlsx). A new one needs `name` and `category`: rooms, doors, windows, walls, floors, ceilings, roofs, columns, structural columns, footings, beams, strip footings, components, stairs, ramps, railings or levels, or `multicategory`, as Revit's Multi-Category Schedule: a row for each element of `categories` (["walls", "doors"…]; none, every built one but rooms, levels and masses), with the fields they share (Category, Family, Type, Level, Count, Width, Height, Length, Thickness, Area: a wall's length by its height, a door's width by its height; Material: its type's structure layer's, a run's type's, a family's), each empty where its category has none; `category` alone reads its own (Room Schedule, Door Schedule, Window Schedule, Wall Schedule, Floor Schedule, Level Schedule, each the project's once changed). `fields`: its columns, in order, each a field's name (`available` lists them: its category's own, Count, project parameters, a component's family's parameters) or {name, formula?, kind?: number|length|area|yesno, heading?, total?}; with a formula, a calculated field worked out from the row's other fields as a family's formulas are (lengths in mm, areas in m²; `Area * 120`); `total` sums it in a totals row. `

args += ['--cmd', 'elements {"category":"viewport"}']

content.content:
reinforce | {host | hosts: [id, …], preset?, cover?, grade?, grade_stirrup?, clearance?, …} bars by rules for a beam, a column, a footing or a floor: the engineer says how many, how thick and how far apart (no standard's number sets them) and it lays them inside the cover and checks that they fit, saying what to change. All: `cover` (mm: one number, or {top, bottom, sides}, top and bottom the faces of a beam, a footing or a floor and the ends of a column; else the host's Cobrimento or ConcreteCover parameter), `grade` (CA-50), `grade_stirrup` (the stirrups' and ties'), `clearance` (least mm between bars; their thickness, at least 20, unless told). A spacing is the most between bars: they are spread evenly, so the last is where the first is from the other end. Beam: `bottom` and `top` {count, diameter, hook?} (`hook`, the straight leg in mm turned up from the bottom bars and down from the top ones at both ends, or {start, end}); `bottom.bent` {count, angle?, top?} bends `count` of the inner bottom bars up at each end (layer `bent`): they run `top` mm along the top face from each end (a fifth of the length unless told), slope down `angle` degrees (15 to 75, 45 unless told) and run along the bott

wire_type | {name?, material?: copper|aluminium, temperature?, insulation?, note?, sizes?: [{section, ampacity, label?}], rename?, delete?: true} a wire type of the project's electrical settings: a conductor's `material`, working `temperature` (°C) and `insulation`, and its table, `sizes`: the `section` of each row in mm² (smallest first, never less than the row before) and the `ampacity` it carries in amperes, with a `label` for how its standard names it (12 AWG). Giving `sizes` replaces the table. `note` says where the ampacities come from. Without `name`, lists them

symbol_set | {set: arei, names?: en|nl|fr} loads a set of families that are plan symbols and nothing else, each of one type `Standard` with no forms: `arei` is the Belgian AREI/RGIE's graphical symbols (Table 2.23: switches, sockets, light points, appliances, sources, domotics, protection), 76 families, switches in the switch category, sockets in outlet, luminaires in lighting and the rest generic. `names` is the language of their names, English, Dutch or French as the source prints them; as given none, French in a French project and English otherwise. A family the project has by that name stays as it is, so loading twice changes nothing; the reply lists `loaded` and `kept`. Place them as components

units | {length?: mm|cm|m|in|ft|ft-in} how drawings, schedules and the desktop show lengths, and read typed ones: millimetres, centimetres, metres, fractional inches, decimal feet, or feet and fractional inches (to 1/16"); areas in m², or ft² with inches and feet. The model, and every command, keep millimetres

standard | {set?: nbr|iso|ansi|eu|jis, adapt_all?: bool, adapt_line_weights?: bool, adapt_object_styles?: bool, adapt_units?: bool} configures the project's technical standard (NBR, ISO, ANSI, EU, JIS) and adapts line weights (pens), sheet layouts, object styles, and dimensioning conventions. NBR includes NBR 16861, NBR 16752, NBR 17006, NBR 17067, NBR 17068, and NBR 6492. The numbers each standard sets (margins, folds, pens, per-category pens) came with the contribution that added them and have not been checked against the standards named. Without `set`, reports the current standard and available standards

drain_size | {units?, fixtures?: {wc?, lav?, sink?, shower?, laundry?}, role?: branch|main|stack, slope?, floors?, min_dn?} the DN of a sanitary drain as NBR 8160 asks, by the fixture units (UHC) it carries: `units`, or `fixtures` counted (Tabela 3: a water closet 6 UHC and DN 100, a lavatory 1 and 40, a sink 3 and 50, a shower 2 and 40, a laundry tub 3 and 40; the drain is never smaller than the fixtures' own). `role`: a `branch` (ramal de esgoto, Tabela 5, the default), a `main` (subcoletor or coletor predial, Tabela 7 by `slope`, a fraction, 0.01 by default; DN 100 at least) or a `stack` (tubo de queda, Tabela 6 by the building's `floors`, up to three or more). `min_dn` is the largest drain flowing into it. Replies with the `dn`, what it carries (`capacity`) and the `minimum_dn` the fixtures ask. A blank in the standard's table means not allowed: DN 100 and 150 carry nothing in a building drain at 0.5 %, and a branch or a building drain never borrows the other's table. For a `main` every fixture given counts, where item 5.1.4.2 counts only the largest fixture of each bathroom in a residential building: pass `units` already reduced to follow it. It has no shortcut: Revit has no tool for it. I

water_size | {fixtures?: {wc, lav, sink, shower, laundry: count}, flow?, method?: weights|sum, dn?, length?, fittings?: {elbow90, elbow45, tee_through, tee_side, gate, globe, check: count}, pressure?, rise?} a cold water pipe of PVC soldável as NBR 5626 asks. The flow is `flow` (L/s), or the design flow of the `fixtures` by the `method` the project chooses: weights (the empirical method, Q = 0.3 √ΣP, never more than the fixtures' own flows; the default) or sum (every fixture at once). The fixture flows and weights are Tigre's (Manual Técnico, page 198), not the standard's; `wc` is the WC with a flush tank only (a flush-valve WC is not in the table here). Without `dn` it replies the smallest DN chosen by speed alone (3 m/s at most; the pressure is not used to choose it); with `dn`, whether that pipe keeps the speed. The head loss is Darcy-Weisbach (Colebrook, PVC at 20 °C) over `length` (mm) plus the equivalent length of the `fittings`; with `pressure` (kPa, dynamic, upstream) and `rise` (mm, up) it replies the pressure left at the end, 10 kPa at least at a point of use, and `ok` covers both; without `pressure` `ok` is the speed alone (`ok_covers` says which). It has no shortcut: Revit has no to

storm_size | {kind: downpipe|horizontal, area?, rainfall?, flow?, outlet?: edge|funnel, gutter?, length?, slope?, inside?} a storm drain as NBR 10844 asks. The flow is `flow` (L/min), or the rain on `area` (m², as the standard counts a roof) at `rainfall` (mm/h; 150 by default, which the standard allows for up to 100 m² only: above that `rainfall` is required): Q = I·A/60. A `downpipe` (condutor vertical) takes the inner diameter of the standard's Figure 3 abacuses by Q, the water depth in the gutter `gutter` (50 to 100 mm), its `length` (mm, 0.3 m or more) and the gutter's `outlet` (edge: sharp-edged, the default; funnel); 70 mm inside at least. A `horizontal` drain takes Manning at two thirds full (n 0.011, PVC only, from the standard's Table 2) at its `slope` (a fraction, 0.005 at least): the inner diameter it needs, and with `inside` (mm) whether that pipe carries the flow. Off the abacuses (more than 150 mm inside) nothing is read. A key that does not apply to the `kind`, or `flow` together with `area`, is an error. It has no shortcut: Revit has no tool for it. It changes nothing

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""margins.py [-m]: for each standard and sheet size, the middle and corner placement of schedules."""
import json, subprocess, sys, tempfile, shutil
ORIG = '/workspace/executable'
MINE = '/workspace/.claude/worktrees/agent-aed8172cff8d68ba7/target/release/bimcraft-cli'
exe = MINE if '-m' in sys.argv else ORIG
stds = ['iso', 'nbr', 'ansi', 'eu', 'jis']
sizes = ['A0', 'A1', 'A2', 'A3', 'A4', 'ARCH A', 'ARCH B', 'ARCH C', 'ARCH D', 'ARCH E', 'ARCH E1', 'ANSI A', 'ANSI B', 'ANSI C', 'ANSI D', 'ANSI E', 'LETTER', 'TABLOID', 'LEDGER']
for std in stds:
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='m', dir='/tmp/views-a/scratch')
    args = [exe, 'run', '--cmd', 'standard {"set":"%s"}' % std, '--cmd', 'sheet {"number":"DEF"}']
    for i, s in enumerate(sizes):
        a = 'M%d' % i
        b = 'C%d' % i
        args += ['--cmd', 'sheet %s' % json.dumps({"number": a, "size": s}), '--cmd', 'sheet %s' % json.dumps({"number": b, "size": s})]
    args += ['--cmd', 'elements {"category":"sheet"}']
    names = ["Room Schedule", "Door Schedule", "Window Schedule", "Wall Schedule", "Floor Schedule", "Level Schedule"]
    p = subprocess.run(args, cwd=d, capture_output=True, timeout=300)
    out = [x for x in p.stdout.decode().strip().split('\n') if x]
    j = json.loads(out[-1])
    dflt = [e for e in j['elements'] if e['number'] == 'DEF'][0]
    print('==', std, 'default sheet size', dflt['size'], dflt['paper'])
    shutil.rmtree(d)
    for i, s in enumerate(sizes):
        d = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='m', dir='/tmp/views-a/scratch')
        args = [exe, 'run', '--cmd', 'standard {"set":"%s"}' % std]
        args += ['--cmd', 'sheet %s' % json.dumps({"number": "M", "size": s}), '--cmd', 'sheet %s' % json.dumps({"number": "C", "size": s})]
        args += ['--cmd', 'place {"sheet":"M","view":"Room Schedule"}']
        args += ['--cmd', 'place {"sheet":"C","view":"Door Schedule","at":[5000,5000]}']
        args += ['--cmd', 'place {"sheet":"C","view":"Level Schedule"}']
        args += ['--cmd', 'elements {"category":"viewport"}', '--cmd', 'elements {"category":"sheet"}']
        p = subprocess.run(args, cwd=d, capture_output=True, timeout=300)
        out = [x for x in p.stdout.decode().strip().split('\n') if x]
        try:
            vps = json.loads(out[-2])['elements']
            sh = json.loads(out[-1])['elements'][0]
            W, H = sh['paper']
            mid = vps[0]['at']
            cor = vps[2]['at']; csz = vps[2]['size']
            x1 = cor[0] + csz[0] / 2; y1 = cor[1] + csz[1] / 2
            x0 = 2 * mid[0] - x1; y0 = 2 * mid[1] - y1
            print('%-8s %-8s paper %-16s mid %-14s area x %.2f..%.2f (W-%.2f) y %.2f..%.2f (H-%.2f)' % (std, s, [W, H], mid, x0, x1, W - x1, y0, y1, H - y1))
        except Exception as e:
            print(std, s, 'ERR', out[-3:], p.stderr.decode())
        shutil.rmtree(d)

import json, math, subprocess, tempfile, shutil, sys
ORIG = '/workspace/executable'
# two walls joined at (10000,0): first along +x, second turning back by angle t (interior angle t)
for t in [10, 14, 15, 16, 20, 25, 28, 29, 30, 31, 35, 40, 45, 60, 90, 120, 150, 170, 179]:
    r = math.radians(t)
    p2 = [10000 - 10000 * math.cos(r), 10000 * math.sin(r)]
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='j', dir='/tmp/views-a/scratch')
    args = [ORIG, 'run', '--cmd', 'wall %s' % json.dumps({"points": [[0, 0], [10000, 0], p2]}), '--cmd', 'crop {"view":"Level 1"}']
    p = subprocess.run(args, cwd=d, capture_output=True)
    out = [x for x in p.stdout.decode().strip().split('\n') if x]
    c = json.loads(out[-1])['crop']
    xmax = c[1][0] - 1000; ymin = c[0][1] + 1000
    # mitre point for the outer faces (right side of first wall y=-100)
    # second wall dir
    dx, dy = p2[0] - 10000, p2[1]
    l = math.hypot(dx, dy); ux, uy = dx / l, dy / l
    # right normal of second wall
    rx, ry = uy, -ux
    # outer face of wall 2: points q with (q - (10000,0)) . (rx,ry) = 100 ; with y=-100
    # (x-10000)*rx + (-100)*ry = 100 -> x = 10000 + (100 + 100*ry)/rx
    mx = 10000 + (100 + 100 * ry) / rx if abs(rx) > 1e-12 else float('nan')
    print('angle %5.1f  xmax %.3f ymin %.3f  mitre x %.3f  mitre len %.1f' % (t, xmax, ymin, mx, math.hypot(mx - 10000, 100)))
    shutil.rmtree(d)

import json, math, subprocess, tempfile, shutil, sys
ORIG = '/workspace/executable'
# arc walls from (0,0) to (L,0) turning `a` degrees CCW: bulge downward (to the right). Measure min y of bbox.
cases = [(10000, 90), (10000, 180), (10000, 60), (10000, 30), (6000, 90), (3000, 90), (20000, 90), (10000, 120), (10000, 270), (1000, 90), (10000, 10)]
for L, a in cases:
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='a', dir='/tmp/views-a/scratch')
    args = [ORIG, 'run', '--cmd', 'wall %s' % json.dumps({"points": [[0, 0], [L, 0]], "arc": a}), '--cmd', 'elevation {"facing":"south"}', '--cmd', 'elements {"category":"elevation"}']
    p = subprocess.run(args, cwd=d, capture_output=True)
    out = [x for x in p.stdout.decode().strip().split('\n') if x]
    try:
        e = json.loads(out[-1])['elements'][0]
    except Exception:
        print(L, a, out, p.stderr.decode()); continue
    ymin = e['start'][1] + 3000
    t = math.radians(a)
    r = L / (2 * math.sin(t / 2))
    # centre: left of a->b by h = r cos(t/2) (up), for CCW
    cy = r * math.cos(t / 2)
    ro = r + 100
    # lowest point of the outer face circle
    exact = cy - ro
    # fit n: vertex angles a0 + t*i/n from start angle
    a0 = math.atan2(0 - cy, 0 - L / 2)
    best = []
    for n in range(1, 400):
        ys = [cy + ro * math.sin(a0 + t * i / n) for i in range(n + 1)]
        if abs(min(ys) - ymin) < 1e-6:
            best.append(n)
    # candidate formula with tol on centre radius
    def nfor(tol, rr):
        return math.ceil(t / (2 * math.acos(1 - tol / rr)))
    print('L %6d arc %4d r %9.2f ymin %.6f exact %.6f  n fits %s  n(tol1,r)=%d n(tol1,ro)=%d n(.5,r)=%d' % (L, a, r, ymin, exact, best[:6], nfor(1, r), nfor(1, ro), nfor(0.5, r)))
    shutil.rmtree(d)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""pdfdump.py file.pdf: decompress the page content and summarize: each path's stroke width, bbox and
points. Text glyphs (stroke widths matching lettering) are grouped into runs by line width and baseline."""
import zlib, re, sys
d = open(sys.argv[1], 'rb').read()
i = d.index(b'stream') + 7
j = d.index(b'endstream')
s = zlib.decompress(d[i:j]).decode('latin1')
if '-raw' in sys.argv:
    print(s)
    sys.exit()
lines = s.split('\n')
paths = []
for l in lines:
    m = re.search(r'([\d.]+) w', l)
    w = float(m.group(1)) if m else None
    nums = re.findall(r'(-?[\d.]+) (-?[\d.]+) [ml]', l)
    pts = [(float(a), float(b)) for a, b in nums]
    kind = 'fill' if l.strip().endswith(' f') else 'stroke'
    if pts:
        xs = [p[0] for p in pts]; ys = [p[1] for p in pts]
        paths.append((w, kind, min(xs), min(ys), max(xs), max(ys), pts, l))
for p in paths:
    w, kind, x0, y0, x1, y1, pts, l = p
    if '-all' in sys.argv or not (w in (1.25, 1.75, 2.5, 3.5, 1.0, 2.0) and kind == 'stroke' and (x1 - x0) < 40 and (y1 - y0) < 40):
        print('%-6s w=%-5s bbox (%.2f,%.2f)-(%.2f,%.2f) n=%d %s' % (kind, w, x0, y0, x1, y1, len(pts), l[:160] if len(pts) <= 5 else ''))
# glyph runs: group text strokes by (w, y range)
runs = {}
for p in paths:
    w, kind, x0, y0, x1, y1, pts, l = p

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""pdfdump.py file.pdf: decompress the page content and summarize: each path's stroke width, bbox and
points. Text glyphs (stroke widths matching lettering) are grouped into runs by line width and baseline."""
import zlib, re, sys
d = open(sys.argv[1], 'rb').read()
i = d.index(b'stream') + 7
j = d.index(b'endstream')
s = zlib.decompress(d[i:j]).decode('latin1')
if '-raw' in sys.argv:
    print(s)
    sys.exit()
lines = s.split('\n')
paths = []
for l in lines:
    m = re.search(r'([\d.]+) w', l)
    w = float(m.group(1)) if m else None
    nums = re.findall(r'(-?[\d.]+) (-?[\d.]+) [ml]', l)
    pts = [(float(a), float(b)) for a, b in nums]
    kind = 'fill' if l.strip().endswith(' f') else 'stroke'
    if pts:
        xs = [p[0] for p in pts]; ys = [p[1] for p in pts]
        paths.append((w, kind, min(xs), min(ys), max(xs), max(ys), pts, l))
for p in paths:

    cos_half = dot(bis, mul(na, -1))
    forms['bisector'] = add(c, mul(bis, h / cos_half))
    # 4: miter vector = (-(na+nb)) * h / (1 + dot(na, nb))
    s = add(na, nb)
    forms['n-sum'] = sub(c, mul(s, h / (1 + dot(na, nb))))
    # 5: from B side
    t = cross(sub(pa, pb), ua) / cross(ub, ua)
    forms['corner-anchored from B'] = add(pb, mul(ub, t))
    # 6: unnormalized directions
    da = sub(c, a0); db = sub(b1, c)
    t = cross(sub(pb, pa), db) / cross(da, db)
    forms['corner-anchored raw'] = add(pa, mul(da, t))
    t = cross(sub(pb2, pa2), db) / cross(da, db)
    forms['far raw'] = add(pa2, mul(da, t))
    # line eq form: n.x = n.p ; solve 2x2
    ra = mul(na, -1); rb = mul(nb, -1)
    ca = dot(ra, c) + h; cb = dot(rb, c) + h
    det = ra[0] * rb[1] - ra[1] * rb[0]
    forms['line eq'] = ((ca * rb[1] - cb * ra[1]) / det, (ra[0] * cb - rb[0] * ca) / det)
    res[k] = forms
for k, forms in res.items():
    print('corner', k, P[k])
    for n, v in forms.items():
        hit = [t for t, tv in targets.items() if tv in v]
        print('   %-24s %r %r %s' % (n, v[0], v[1], hit))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""For each language and schedule category, the number of letters each field's heading has on a sheet."""
import json, subprocess, tempfile, shutil, math, sys
ORIG = '/workspace/executable'
cats = {
    'rooms': ["Number", "Name", "Level", "Area", "Perimeter", "Count", "Unbounded Height", "Volume", "Phase Created", "Phase Demolished", "Design Option"],
    'doors': ["Mark", "Type", "Width", "Height", "Level", "Wall", "Family", "Operation", "Count", "Phase Created", "Phase Demolished", "Design Option"],
    'windows': ["Mark", "Type", "Width", "Height", "Sill", "Level", "Wall", "Family", "Operation", "Count", "Phase Created", "Phase Demolished", "Design Option"],
    'walls': ["Id", "Type", "Level", "Length", "Height", "Thickness", "Count", "Phase Created", "Phase Demolished", "Design Option"],
    'floors': ["Id", "Type", "Level", "Area", "Thickness", "Offset", "Count", "Structural", "Phase Created", "Phase Demolished", "Design Option"],
    'levels': ["Elevation", "Name", "Count"],
}
langs = sys.argv[1:] or ['en', 'pt', 'es', 'sv', 'cs', 'fr', 'nl', 'de', 'it']
result = {}
for l in langs:
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='fc', dir='/tmp/views-a/scratch')
    args = [ORIG, 'run', '--cmd', 'new {"language":"%s"}' % l, '--cmd', 'sheet {"size":"A0","number":"Z"}']
    items = []
    i = 0
    for c, fields in cats.items():
        for f in fields:
            name = 'q%d' % i
            i += 1
            args += ['--cmd', 'schedule %s' % json.dumps({"name": name, "category": c, "fields": [f]})]
            args += ['--cmd', 'place %s' % json.dumps({"sheet": "Z", "view": name, "at": [100, 100]})]
            items.append((c, f))
    args += ['--cmd', 'elements {"category":"viewport"}']
    p = subprocess.run(args, cwd=d, capture_output=True, timeout=300)
    out = [x for x in p.stdout.decode().strip().split('\n') if x]
    if p.stderr:
        print(l, p.stderr.decode()[:300])
    vps = json.loads(out[-1])['elements']
    res = {}
    for (c, f), e in zip(items, vps):
        px = round(e['size'][0] * 5)
        # px = ceil(11.4583 n + 16.875) for n >= 1 (title "qNN" is narrower)
        n = None
        for k in range(0, 200):
            w = 12.5 * (11 * k / 12 - 0.25) + 20 if k > 0 else 20
            if math.ceil(w) == px:
                n = k
                break
        res['%s.%s' % (c, f)] = n if n is not None else ('px', px)
    result[l] = res
    shutil.rmtree(d)
print(json.dumps(result, ensure_ascii=False, indent=0))

    'floors': ["Id", "Type", "Level", "Area", "Thickness", "Offset", "Count", "Structural", "Phase Created", "Phase Demolished", "Design Option"],
    'levels': ["Elevation", "Name", "Count"],
}
langs = sys.argv[1:] or ['en', 'pt', 'es', 'sv', 'cs', 'fr', 'nl', 'de', 'it']
result = {}
for l in langs:
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='fc', dir='/tmp/views-a/scratch')
    args = [ORIG, 'run', '--cmd', 'new {"language":"%s"}' % l, '--cmd', 'sheet {"size":"A0","number":"Z"}']
    items = []
    i = 0
    for c, fields in cats.items():
        for f in fields:
            name = 'q%d' % i
            i += 1
            args += ['--cmd', 'schedule %s' % json.dumps({"name": name, "category": c, "fields": [f]})]
            args += ['--cmd', 'place %s' % json.dumps({"sheet": "Z", "view": name, "at": [100, 100]})]
            items.append((c, f))
    args += ['--cmd', 'elements {"category":"viewport"}']
    p = subprocess.run(args, cwd=d, capture_output=True, timeout=300)
    out = [x for x in p.stdout.decode().strip().split('\n') if x]
    if p.stderr:
        print(l, p.stderr.decode()[:300])
    vps = json.loads(out[-1])['elements']
    res = {}
    for (c, f), e in zip(items, vps):
        px = round(e['size'][0] * 5)
        # px = ceil(11.4583 n + 16.875) for n >= 1 (title "qNN" is narrower)
        n = None
        for k in range(0, 200):
            w = 12.5 * (11 * k / 12 - 0.25) + 20 if k > 0 else 20
            if math.ceil(w) == px:
                n = k
                break
        res['%s.%s' % (c, f)] = n if n is not None else ('px', px)
    result[l] = res
    shutil.rmtree(d)
print(json.dumps(result, ensure_ascii=False, indent=0))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""cellcount.py in.bimcraft [lang]: for each schedule category and field, the widest text (heading or
cell) in letters, from the width of a one-column schedule of it placed on a sheet."""
import json, subprocess, tempfile, shutil, math, sys
ORIG = '/workspace/executable'
cats = {
    'rooms': ["Number", "Name", "Level", "Area", "Perimeter", "Count", "Unbounded Height", "Volume"],
    'doors': ["Mark", "Type", "Width", "Height", "Level", "Wall", "Family", "Operation", "Count"],
    'windows': ["Mark", "Type", "Width", "Height", "Sill", "Level", "Wall", "Family", "Operation", "Count"],
    'walls': ["Id", "Type", "Level", "Length", "Height", "Thickness", "Count"],
    'floors': ["Id", "Type", "Level", "Area", "Thickness", "Offset", "Count", "Structural"],
    'levels': ["Elevation", "Name", "Count"],
}
infile = sys.argv[1]
d = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='cc', dir='/tmp/views-a/scratch')
shutil.copy(infile, d)
import os
args = [ORIG, 'run', os.path.basename(infile), '--cmd', 'sheet {"size":"A0","number":"Z"}']
items = []
i = 0
for c, fields in cats.items():
    for f in fields:
        name = chr(0x3b1 + i) if i < 25 else chr(0x430 + i - 25)
        i += 1
        args += ['--cmd', 'schedule %s' % json.dumps({"name": name, "category": c, "fields": [f]})]
        args += ['--cmd', 'place %s' % json.dumps({"sheet": "Z", "view": name, "at": [100, 100]})]
        items.append((c, f))
args += ['--cmd', 'elements {"category":"viewport"}']
p = subprocess.run(args, cwd=d, capture_output=True, timeout=300)
out = [x for x in p.stdout.decode().strip().split('\n') if x]
if p.stderr:
    print(p.stderr.decode()[:300])
vps = json.loads(out[-1])['elements']
# rows from the schedule replies
rows = {}
k = 0
for line in out[2:]:
    try:
        j = json.loads(line)
    except Exception:
        continue
    if 'rows' in j and 'columns' in j:
        rows[items[k]] = j['rows']
        k += 1
for (c, f), e in zip(items, vps):
    px = round(e['size'][0] * 5)
    h = round(e['size'][1] * 5)
    n = None
    for kk in range(0, 200):
        w = 12.5 * (11 * kk / 12 - 0.25) + 20 if kk > 0 else 20
        if math.ceil(w) == px:
            n = kk
            break
    print('%-8s %-18s letters %-4s rows %d  values %s' % (c, f, n, (h - 75) // 30, [r[0] for r in rows.get((c, f), [])][:6]))
shutil.rmtree(d)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""cellcount.py in.bimcraft [lang]: for each schedule category and field, the widest text (heading or
cell) in letters, from the width of a one-column schedule of it placed on a sheet."""
import json, subprocess, tempfile, shutil, math, sys
ORIG = '/workspace/executable'
cats = {
    'rooms': ["Number", "Name", "Level", "Area", "Perimeter", "Count", "Unbounded Height", "Volume"],
    'doors': ["Mark", "Type", "Width", "Height", "Level", "Wall", "Family", "Operation", "Count"],
    'windows': ["Mark", "Type", "Width", "Height", "Sill", "Level", "Wall", "Family", "Operation", "Count"],
    'walls': ["Id", "Type", "Level", "Length", "Height", "Thickness", "Count"],
    'floors': ["Id", "Type", "Level", "Area", "Thickness", "Offset", "Count", "Structural"],
    'levels': ["Elevation", "Name", "Count"],
}
infile = sys.argv[1]
d = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='cc', dir='/tmp/views-a/scratch')
shutil.copy(infile, d)
import os
args = [ORIG, 'run', os.path.basename(infile), '--cmd', 'sheet {"size":"A0","number":"Z"}']
items = []
i = 0
for c, fields in cats.items():
    for f in fields:
        name = chr(0x3b1 + i) if i < 25 else chr(0x430 + i - 25)
        i += 1
        args += ['--cmd', 'schedule %s' % json.dumps({"name": name, "category": c, "fields": [f]})]
        args += ['--cmd', 'place %s' % json.dumps({"sheet": "Z", "view": name, "at": [100, 100]})]
        items.append((c, f))
args += ['--cmd', 'elements {"category":"viewport"}']
p = subprocess.run(args, cwd=d, capture_output=True, timeout=300)
out = [x for x in p.stdout.decode().strip().split('\n') if x]
if p.stderr:
    print(p.stderr.decode()[:300])
vps = json.loads(out[-1])['elements']
# rows from the schedule replies
rows = {}
k = 0
for line in out[2:]:
    try:
        j = json.loads(line)
    except Exception:
        continue
    if 'rows' in j and 'columns' in j:
        rows[items[k]] = j['rows']
        k += 1
for (c, f), e in zip(items, vps):
    px = round(e['size'][0] * 5)
    h = round(e['size'][1] * 5)
    n = None
    for kk in range(0, 200):
        w = 12.5 * (11 * kk / 12 - 0.25) + 20 if kk > 0 else 20
        if math.ceil(w) == px:
            n = kk
            break
    print('%-8s %-18s letters %-4s rows %d  values %s' % (c, f, n, (h - 75) // 30, [r[0] for r in rows.get((c, f), [])][:6]))
shutil.rmtree(d)

    ('P named Level 2, B too short', [('P', 'name', 'Level 2'), ('B', 'end', [0.0, 0.0])]),
    ('E named A, B too short', [('E', 'name', 'A'), ('B', 'end', [0.0, 0.0])]),
    ('E named Level 1, A blank', [('E', 'name', 'Level 1'), ('A', 'name', '')]),
    ('viewport scale 0, E too short', [('viewport', 'scale', 0.0), ('E', 'end', [0.0, 0.0])]),
    ('A depth 0 and too short', [('A', 'depth', 0.0), ('A', 'end', [0.0, 0.0])]),
    ('A crop [5,1] and depth 0', [('A', 'crop', [5.0, 1.0]), ('A', 'depth', 0.0)]),
    ('A named B (dup), A depth 0', [('B', 'depth', 0.0), ('B', 'name', 'A')]),
    ('level crop bad, B too short', [('Level 1', 'crop', [[5.0, 5.0], [0.0, 0.0]]), ('B', 'end', [0.0, 0.0])]),
    ('P crop bad, B too short', [('P', 'crop', [[5.0, 5.0], [0.0, 0.0]]), ('B', 'end', [0.0, 0.0])]),
    ('S1 number blank, S2 size bad', [('S1', 'number', ' '), ('S2', 'size', 'Q')]),
    ('S2 number S1 and size bad', [('S2', 'number', 'S1'), ('S2', 'size', 'Q')]),
]
for name, changes in cases:
    d = json.loads(json.dumps(d0))
    for who, k, v in changes:
        d['elements'][ids[who]][k] = v
    f = '/tmp/views-a/in/craft.bimcraft'
    json.dump(d, open(f, 'w'), indent=2)
    outs = []
    for exe in [ORIG, os.environ.get('MINE', '/workspace/.claude/worktrees/agent-aed8172cff8d68ba7/target/release/bimcraft-cli')]:

ceiling | {point: [x,y] | boundary: [[x,y],…], openings?: [[[x,y],…],…] | sketch: [[[x,y],[x,y]],…], level?, type?, offset?} a ceiling, its underside `offset` mm (2600) above the level, open through `openings` (holes inside it, apart): in the room around `point`, out to its walls' faces and round the walls standing inside it, or along `boundary`. Reflected ceiling plans show it

shaft | {boundary: [[x,y],…] | sketch: [[[x,y],[x,y]],…], level?, top_level?, height?, base_offset?} a hole through the floors, ceilings and roofs it passes through, from `base_offset` above the level up to the next level, or `height` mm, or up to `top_level`

mass | {boundary: [[x,y],…], level?, top_level?, height?, base_offset?, top?: [[x,y],…], lean?: [dx,dy], name?} a mass, Revit's conceptual volume: the footprint extruded from `base_offset` above the level up to the next level, or `height` mm, or up to `top_level`. With `top`, an outline of as many points as the footprint (twin for twin, running the same way round), it is lofted straight from the footprin

room_separator | {points: [[x,y],…], level?, closed?} room separation lines along `points`, one per segment (`closed` joins the last to the first): they bound rooms as walls do, to split an open space (a living room and its corridor) into rooms, and are nothing else, with no solid, no cut and no area. Returns their ids

beam | {points: [[x,y],…], closed?, type?, level?, offset?, end_offset?, justify?: top|centre|bottom, system?} a beam for each segment of the points: its section the type's (category beam: `width` across, `depth` deep, or round), its `justify` line (top by default) `offset` mm over the level at its start (0: at the level, so it hangs below) and `end_offset` at its end (the same: level), for a single segm

pipe | {points: [[x,y],…], closed?, type?, level?, offset?, end_offset?, justify?: top|centre|bottom, system?} a pipe for each segment of the points: its section the type's (category pipe: round, `width` the outside diameter), its `justify` line (centre by default) `offset` mm over the level at its start (0: at the level) and `end_offset` at its end (the same: level), for a single segment, so a drain fal

duct | {points: [[x,y],…], closed?, type?, level?, offset?, end_offset?, justify?: top|centre|bottom, system?} a duct for each segment of the points: its section the type's (category duct: `width` across by `depth` deep, or round, `width` the diameter), its `justify` line (centre by default) `offset` mm over the level at its start (0: at the level) and `end_offset` at its end (the same: level), for a sin

stair | {start: [x,y], end?: [x,y] | angle?, level?, top_level?, height?, width?, riser?, tread?, landings?: [{at, turn?}, …], railings?} a stair from the middle of its first riser at `start`, climbing toward `end` (or `angle` degrees) up to the next level: as many risers as keep each at most `riser` mm (180), treads `tread` deep (280), `width` wide (1000). One straight run, as long as that makes it; or w

ramp | {start: [x,y], end?: [x,y] | angle?, level?, top_level?, height?, width?, slope?, landings?: [{at, turn?}, …], railings?} a ramp from the middle of its foot at `start`, climbing toward `end` (or `angle` degrees) up to the next level, or `height` mm, `width` wide (1200), at `slope` percent (8.33, 1 in 12), as long as that makes it; with landings `at` mm up, turning as a stair's do, and with `railin

railing | {host: a stair or a ramp, side?: left|right, type?} | {path: [[x,y],…], level?, base_offset?, type?} a railing along the stair's or the ramp's sides (both, or the one going up it on `side`), 50 mm in from its edges and climbing with it, going where it goes; or along `path`, `base_offset` mm above the level. Its type sets how high its rail stands over what it runs along, and how far apart its balus

component | {family, type?, at: [x,y], level?, angle?, offset?, mirrored?, params?: {parameter: value}} a family's type placed, its first by default: at a point on a level, turned `angle` degrees counter-clockwise, `offset` mm up from the level, and with `mirrored` flipped across its own x axis; `params` sets its instance parameters (`modify` merges into them, a null taking one back to the family's)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Measures how many letters a level's head has in a section, for elevations in each length unit:
the level is named one letter, the section sees nothing, so the width is its line, margins and head."""
import json, subprocess, tempfile, shutil, math, sys
ORIG = '/workspace/executable'
units = ['mm', 'cm', 'm', 'in', 'ft', 'ft-in']
elevs = [0.0, 1.0, 3000.0, 1234.5, -2500.0, 25.4, 304.8, 12.7, 1.5875, 99999.0, 0.4]
for u in units:
    row = []
    for z in elevs:
        d = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='h', dir='/tmp/views-a/scratch')
        args = [ORIG, 'run', '--cmd', 'units {"length":"%s"}' % u, '--cmd', 'modify {"id":100000,"name":"A","elevation":%r}' % z,
                '--cmd', 'modify {"id":100001,"name":"B","elevation":%r}' % (z + 0.0001 if z >= 0 else z - 0.0001),
                '--cmd', 'section {"start":[0,30000],"end":[100,30000]}', '--cmd', 'sheet {}',
                '--cmd', 'place {"sheet":"A101","view":"Section 1","scale":1}', '--cmd', 'elements {"category":"viewport"}']
        p = subprocess.run(args, cwd=d, capture_output=True, text=True)
        out = [x for x in p.stdout.strip().split('\n') if x]
        try:
            w = json.loads(out[-1])['elements'][0]['size'][0]
            px = round(w * 5)
            head = px - 500 - 120 - 12
            n = None
            for k in range(1, 40):
                if math.ceil(500 + 120 + 12 + 10 / 12 * (11 * (k - 1) + 8)) == px:
                    n = k
            row.append('%s:%s' % (z, n))
        except Exception as e:
            row.append('%s:ERR %s' % (z, p.stderr.strip()[:80]))
        shutil.rmtree(d)
    print(u, ' '.join(row))

import math, itertools
P = [(0.0, 0.0), (7071.0678, 7071.0678), (2828.4271, 11313.7085), (-4242.6407, 4242.6407)]
h = 100.0
def unit_div(v):
    l = math.sqrt(v[0] * v[0] + v[1] * v[1]); return (v[0] / l, v[1] / l)
def unit_inv(v):
    l = math.sqrt(v[0] * v[0] + v[1] * v[1]); r = 1 / l; return (v[0] * r, v[1] * r)
def sub(a, b): return (a[0] - b[0], a[1] - b[1])
def add(a, b): return (a[0] + b[0], a[1] + b[1])
def mul(a, k): return (a[0] * k, a[1] * k)
def cross(a, b): return a[0] * b[1] - a[1] * b[0]
targets = [None, ('x', 7212.48915623731), ('y', 11455.129856237309), ('x', -4384.06205623731)]
targets0 = ('y', -141.421356237309)
targets = [targets0] + targets[1:]
for uname, unit in [('div', unit_div), ('inv', unit_inv)]:
    hits = {}
    for k in range(4):
        a0, c, b1 = P[k - 1], P[k], P[(k + 1) % 4]
        # walls A: a0->c, B: c->b1; CCW box: right faces are outside
        ua = unit(sub(c, a0)); ub = unit(sub(b1, c))
        na = (-ua[1], ua[0]); nb = (-ub[1], ub[0])
        # right faces: as two points each
        p1 = add(a0, mul(na, -h)); p2 = add(c, mul(na, -h))
        q1 = add(c, mul(nb, -h)); q2 = add(b1, mul(nb, -h))
        forms = {}
        r = sub(p2, p1); s_ = sub(q2, q1)
        den = cross(r, s_)
        for an, (pa, rr) in {'p1+r': (p1, r), 'p2-r': (p2, mul(r, -1))}.items():
            for bn, (qa, ss) in {'q1+s': (q1, s_), 'q2-s': (q2, mul(s_, -1))}.items():
                dd = cross(rr, ss)
                if dd == 0: continue
                t = cross(sub(qa, pa), ss) / dd
                forms['A %s B %s' % (an, bn)] = add(pa, mul(rr, t))
                u_ = cross(sub(qa, pa), rr) / dd
                forms['B %s A %s' % (bn, an)] = add(qa, mul(ss, u_))
        # line equation forms: a x + b y = c
        def line_eq(p, q):
            a = q[1] - p[1]; b = p[0] - q[0]; cc = a * p[0] + b * p[1]
            return a, b, cc
        A1, B1, C1 = line_eq(p1, p2); A2, B2, C2 = line_eq(q1, q2)
        det = A1 * B2 - A2 * B1
        forms['eq'] = ((B2 * C1 - B1 * C2) / det, (A1 * C2 - A2 * C1) / det)
        axis, tv = targets[k]
        for n_, v in forms.items():
            val = v[0] if axis == 'x' else v[1]
            if val == tv:
                hits.setdefault(n_, []).append(k)
    print(uname, {k: v for k, v in hits.items()})

content.text:
VIEWS-A is done and committed. The six commands, the model checks for my categories, `element_view` and `dependents` are all in. My regression files give 929 identical results out of 969 when run against the original. Every remaining difference is either a command other sub-agents haven't built yet, or a known approximation listed below.

**Branch:** `worktree-agent-aed8172cff8d68ba7`, last commit `3ead0d7` (13 commits on top of `9de3863`). Files: `src/views/sections.rs`, `src/views/sheets.rs`, `src/views/sheets/paper.rs` (new), `src/views/plans.rs`, `src/views/plans/shows.rs` (new).

**Per command, what matches:**
- **section**: parameter checks and their order, default names in all 9 languages, saved JSON, replies, undo labels. `elements` adds `length` and `looking`, computed as the original does (multiplying by 1/length, no `-0`).
- **elevation**: `facing`, `at`, `start`/`end`, `depth`, `name`, "the four not there yet" (one made replies `{id,name}`, several `{ids}`), the 4 names in all languages, "North 2". The box it frames is walls and floors, with mitred L-corners (no mitre when it would reach past a wall thickness) and arcs cut into 1 mm chords; exact for axis-aligned walls and single diagonal walls.
  - Doesn't match: joined non-axis-aligned walls (rotated boxes, angled chains, acute corners) and arc walls differ in the last 1–2 digits of the saved coordinates. I couldn't find the original's arithmetic for those.
- **sheet**: numbering A101…, "Unnamed" in all languages, sizes (A0–A4, ARCH A–E1, ANSI A–E, LETTER/TABLOID/LEDGER, any case). `elements` adds `paper` and `viewports`.
- **place**: matches everywhere I tested:
  - views by name or id; schedules by any language's name, created in the project's language; `{3D}` created with `azimuth`/`elevation`; scale from the view, its template or its dependent's parent; every error.
  - default position: per-standard margins (iso/eu/jis/nbr/ansi, A4 special), right of the views there or else the top-right corner, with the original's float results.
  - viewport `size` (computed from the original's rendered PDFs): plans, sections/elevations with level heads in the project's length units, the 3D view's picture (capped at 4096 px), and schedules lettered in single-stroke capitals, with translated heading lengths per language.
  - Doesn't match: room Area/Perimeter cells (no room boundaries), schedule filters/grouping, and the exact 3D shape of stairs and furniture.
- **crop**:
  - plans: an explicit region, `null`, or "what it shows" (±1000 mm, rounded to the micron), which takes in model, marks, grids, rooms, runs, railings, tags and annotation;
  - sections: `[bottom, top]`, with the line moved to the region and only text notes and spots kept in place;
  - it always makes an undo step, and all its error texts match.
- **duplicate_view**: duplicate, detailing (copies every annotation kind the original copies, `view` inserted in the right field order, region sketch parts renumbered) and dependent; names in all languages; all errors.

**Checks:** one pass in id order, so the first error matches the original's. Covers names (another view, a level's name), section/elevation length, depth and crop, plan crops, plan view level and parent, sheet number and size, viewport scale/sheet/view and "a view goes on one sheet". I verified the ordering on hand-edited files. I also added the 3D view's ±89° elevation check, because `place` can set it; VIEW3D may add the same check, which is harmless.

**Functions exposed:**
- `plans::dependents(pr, gone)`: the extra ids that go, in id order. I confirmed it against the original's `delete` output with a temporary hook (since reverted), across 14 cases. EDIT should delete `gone` plus this list.
- `plans::shows`: `plan_shows`, `section_frame`, `solids`, `wall_outlines`, `walls_and_floors_box`, `view3d_extent`, `host_point`.
- `sheets::paper`: `view_size`, `viewport_size`, `length_text`, `paper_size`, `schedule_of`, `schedule_name`.
- `sections::numbered_name` / `word_name`, `plans::find_any_view`, `plans::insert_in_order`, `sheets::scale_in_force`.

**Problems outside my files (not changed by me):**
- The original runs the full model check when it opens a file (`open: <path>: section 100003: too short (0 mm)`); our loader only checks point clouds. It also rejects dangling GUIDs and wrongly shaped fields on open.
- `basic.rs` `level_word` gives German "Ebene", but the original names German levels "Geschoss 3".
- `common::find_view` behaves differently from the original, so I use my own lookups:
  - it accepts GUIDs without dashes, which the original rejects;
  - for `duplicate_view` the original doesn't find sheets by number;
  - `place` rejects id strings and `{3d}` in lowercase, which `find_view` accepts.
- EDIT's `delete` should error with "delete: no element N" for a missing id.

Regression files and tools are in `/tmp/views-a/` (`reg/*.txt`, `regall.py`, `q.py`, input projects in `in/`).
